4.speaker: Player
4.text: “Of course, Chancellor Hegel. It was a pleasure.”

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: He leaned back in his chair and took another puff from the pipe.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: As the assistant collected the empty glasses, he whispered into Hegel's ear.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: Hegel's eyes widened and he clenched his fists in anger.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: We shook hands and Hegel left in a hurry.

11.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
11.text: “Thank you for the offer, but no.”

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: He composed himself and smiled at me.

13.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
13.text: “Mr. Rayne, I'm afraid you will have to excuse me. There is a matter I need to attend to.”

14.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
14.text: “Have a good day and enjoy Haelm.”

16.speaker: Player
16.text: “Is there anything I can help with?”

19.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
19.text: “If you will excuse me for one minute.”

20.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
20.text: “You are answering my question with a question.”

24.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
24.text: “Thankfully, we in Valgsland have now cut off the head of the snake called imperialism.”

25.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
25.text: “Mr. Rayne. Welcome to Valgsland. It is good to finally meet with you.”

28.speaker: Player
28.text: “It's a pleasure to finally meet with you, Chancellor Hegel.”

30.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
30.text: “Does this have anything to do with the growing threat of Rumburg?”

31.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
31.text: “A blunt answer. I like it. It gives me confidence.”

33.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
33.text: “No country in this world is completely isolated.”

34.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
34.text: “This was made in 1776 by the famous Valgslandian painter, Otto Kiebern.”

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: The assistants brought two more shots. We drank them in one go.

42.speaker: Narrator
42.text: I looked at the painting. It must've been over five meters tall. It was a battle scene. On the left side there were banners carried by Valgs; on the right, Sords.

44.speaker: Narrator
44.text: Countless spears formed a triangle at the center. The sky was red from the blood.

46.speaker: Player
46.text: “Thank you for the offer, but there is only so much vodka I can drink before lunch.”

47.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
47.text: “But so far, you haven't done much to justify such an alignment."

50.speaker: Player
50.text: “We don't need external threats to make a deal with one of our oldest neighbors.”

52.speaker: Player
52.text: “Absolutely not. Sordland can defend itself just fine.”

54.speaker: Narrator
54.text: We clinked the glasses and did our shots.

55.speaker: Narrator
55.text: We shook hands and he pulled me in for a hug.

57.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
57.text: “So you want to keep improving your economy after all those long years of recession.”

59.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
59.text: “So you want to get rid of that recession of yours then.”

60.speaker: Player
60.text: “It is a reminder. One misstep and we are back to painting the world with more blood.”

63.speaker: Player
63.text: “I think that we have come far. After all, we are standing here side by side instead of facing each other on a battlefield.”

64.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
64.text: “This time, Sords and Valgs will stand side by side.”

65.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
65.text: “As the leaders of this world, we must be careful, Mr. Rayne.”

68.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
68.text: “This time we will not be on opposing sides of history.”

69.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
69.text: “This time, Sords and Valgs will stand side by side.”

70.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
70.text: “We can do so much more through unity, Mr. Rayne.”

72.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
72.text: “If your actions matched your words, this could've gone differently. But let's not talk about what could have been."

73.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
73.text: “Yes! This time we will not be on opposing sides.”

74.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
74.text: “We have much to gain from an alliance between our two nations.”

75.speaker: Player
75.text: “Why should you not? What do you have to lose?”

76.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
76.text: “I have been watching Sordland's development with worry over the last few years.”

78.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
78.text: “Especially around those who are willing and ready to do precisely that.”

79.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
79.text: “It would be a bit quick, but I am not opposed either.”

81.speaker: Narrator
81.text: He turned to me and put his hand on my shoulder.

84.speaker: Player
84.text: “Since we have come this far, I am not opposed to the idea of an alliance.”

85.speaker: Player
85.text: “I know you are a busy man. Thank you for your time today, Chancellor Hegel.”

86.speaker: Player
86.text: “I want an alliance, Chancellor Hegel. I want to revive the brotherhood of old!”

88.speaker: Player
88.text: “It is the first step towards improving the ties between our nations.”

89.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
89.text: “To me, this painting tells me how far we have come. Sords and Valgs might have had troubles in the past, but ultimately, we are brothers.”

90.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
90.text: “No two countries in the world understand each other more.”

91.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
91.text: “I have been watching Sordland's development with worry over the last few years.”

92.speaker: Player
92.text: “More trade means more money circulation. Undoubtedly it will help both of our nations' economies.”

93.speaker: Narrator
93.text: He took another puff from his pipe.

95.speaker: Narrator
95.text: We gulped down the shots after clinking.

98.speaker: Player
98.text: “It is great to hear these important words coming from you.”

99.speaker: Narrator
99.text: The assistant immediately showed up with two shots of vodka.

100.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
100.text: “Although I would appreciate the support, as you said, our matters are not yours.”

101.speaker: Player
101.text: “Let's hope we can stay that way.”

102.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
102.text: “If you say that, I believe you.”

103.speaker: Player
103.text: “I want to align Sordland closer with the CSP.”

104.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
104.text: “Forgive me, Mr. Rayne. I was trying to figure out your intentions.”

108.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
108.text: “We have achieved a lot today, Mr. Rayne.”

111.speaker: Narrator
111.text: He nodded and pointed towards another painting that was almost as large as the first one. A burning city was depicted. Looking closer, I realized it was Conriat.

116.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
116.text: “You are making trade deals with Agnolians, our sworn rivals.”

118.speaker: Narrator
118.text: He pointed towards another painting that was almost as large as the first one. A burning city was depicted. Looking closer, I realized it was Conriat.

121.speaker: Narrator
121.text: The strong bite of alcohol turned into a sweeter aftertaste.

123.speaker: Narrator
123.text: He leaned back in his chair and took another puff from the pipe.

124.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
124.text: “The most shameful event in all of Valgslandian history. The scars of it must still sting.”

125.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
125.text: “But I can't risk international backlash. If I have you... if I have Sordland behind our cause, everything will be easier.”

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: We clinked the glasses and drank our shots.

130.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
130.text: “This is not your battle, after all.”

133.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
133.text: “In Valgsland we drink on a contract, Mr. Rayne.”

134.speaker: Player
134.text: “Past is past. We need to look into the future.”

135.speaker: Player
135.text: “We shouldn't bear the sins of our forefathers.”

136.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
136.text: “Don't worry. I don't wish to pull Sordland into this conflict in any way.”

137.speaker: Player
137.text: “We will never forget the extremely shameful display by the Valgslandian navy. ”

138.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
138.text: “Very well. Then you have ended your chances of achieving this deal.”

142.speaker: Narrator
142.text: He called an assistant nearby. A moment later the assistant returned with two shots of vodka.

143.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
143.text: “I will accept the deal on the basis of your sincerity.”

144.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
144.text: “I am planning on invading Heljiland to save Valgslandian citizens from the clutches of the murderous Agnolians.”

145.speaker: Narrator
145.text: He called an assistant nearby. A moment later the assistant returned with two shots of vodka.

146.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
146.text: “We have achieved a lot today, Mr. Rayne.”

148.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
148.text: “We will never forget the sins of our fathers.”

151.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
151.text: “That is precisely what I am trying to do, Mr. Rayne.”

152.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
152.text: “If they want to mess with Valgsland, they will see our might!”

153.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
153.text: “Mr. Rayne. Since we have signed our trade deal, I will be open with you.”

155.speaker: Narrator
155.text: The strong bite of alcohol turned into a sweeter aftertaste.

163.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
163.text: “The window for diplomatic action is closing, Mr. Rayne.”

164.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
164.text: “I am not sure how much longer I can show restraint.”

165.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
165.text: “But understanding your own position is a virtue.”

168.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
168.text: “I have to protect my nation, and to do so I will concern myself with whatever I want. You have no say in that.”

169.speaker: Narrator
169.text: He stepped away with the guard while I looked around. I saw a more recent painting, depicting the upheaval of farmers against an aristocrat.

172.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
172.text: “I am glad to see you are making progress in fixing the situation created by your predecessor.”

173.speaker: Narrator
173.text: Hegel's loud voice echoed in the empty halls.

176.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
176.text: “Imagine they did that to Sordish people. What would you do?”

177.speaker: Player
177.text: “I would slaughter them just like they slaughtered us!”

178.speaker: Player
178.text: “Chancellor Hegel. I urge you to remain calm on the matter. No one wants war.”

179.speaker: Player
179.text: “I would approach the matter diplomatically. Surely a middle way can be found.”

181.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
181.text: “If I accept this deal, I will lose face with my people.”

182.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
182.text: “There is something you can do for me to make this deal work.”

183.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
183.text: “But, you do have a point. Why should we not, indeed?”

184.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
184.text: “I know the details of the deal already, but to sum it up...”

185.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
185.text: “Give the miners what they want. As for the director of the company, I want him to face a trial for undermining the workers of Valgsland. Relay it to the Minister of Justice at once!”

186.speaker: Narrator
186.text: He leaned back in his chair and took another puff from his pipe.

187.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
187.text: “No one can exploit our people and expect to get away with it.”

188.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
188.text: “What makes you think that Valgsland, a seafaring nation, requires Sordish fishing output?”

189.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
189.text: “If they want to mess with Valgsland, they will see our might!”

191.speaker: Narrator
191.text: After receiving the order, the guard hastily left. Hegel walked over to me.

192.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
192.text: “What makes you think that Valgsland, a nation rich with wheat farms, requires Sordish wheat?”

193.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
193.text: “The more nations we have on our side against the Agnolians, the better.”

194.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
194.text: “What makes you think that Valgsland, a nation with plenty of its own coal mines, requires Sordish coal?”

195.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
195.text: “What makes you think that Valgsland, a nation with considerable tungsten reserves, requires Sordish tungsten?”

196.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
196.text: “I have had it with those damn Agnolians claiming *our* land as their own.”

197.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
197.text: “As if that's not enough, they kill my people in their homes in Heljiland! Slaughtering them like mere cattle.”

198.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
198.text: “Sorry about that. You know how it is.”

199.speaker: Player
199.text: “Let's move on with the scheduled program.”

200.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
200.text: “I am not sure how much longer I can show restraint.”

203.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
203.text: “The window for diplomatic action is closing, Mr. Rayne.”

204.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
204.text: “For the sake of our conversation, let's say that there is something I want.”

208.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
208.text: “A director of a foreign joint-venture mining corporation decided not to pay his miners their salary for two consecutive months. He will be handled.”

209.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
209.text: “Mr. Rayne. Are you not reading your newspapers?”

211.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
211.text: “Now. If you wish to join the CSP, you will have to put more effort into it.”

212.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
212.text: “It also takes strength to be able to overcome your pride and say that you need help.”

215.speaker: Narrator
215.text: The strong bite of alcohol turned into a sweeter aftertaste.

216.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
216.text: “Revolution is a slow process, Mr. Rayne. Slow but sure.”

217.speaker: Narrator
217.text: He picked up the documents that were beside him on the small ornamental coffee table and started going through them.

218.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
218.text: “Since you are so focused on the economic aspect, let me do that too.”

219.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
219.text: “I want Sordland and Valgsland to be closer again as two nations.”

220.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
220.text: “Follow me. We will have a short breakfast.”

221.speaker: Player
221.text: “Why do you want this from me?”

222.speaker: Player
222.text: “I won't meddle in the affairs between Valgsland and Agnolia.”

224.speaker: Player
224.text: “I would slaughter them just like they slaughtered us!”

225.speaker: Player
225.text: “Chancellor Hegel. I urge you to remain calm on the matter. No one wants war.”

226.speaker: Player
226.text: “I would approach the matter diplomatically. Surely a middle way can be found.”

228.speaker: Narrator
228.text: We made our way to the exquisite dining room. I looked around. The tableware and decor was all colored gold, blue and white.

229.speaker: Player
229.text: “Then I will make it worth your while.”

230.speaker: Narrator
230.text: Smoked bear meat, a local delicacy, was served with eggs. After a very delicious meal, we sat down on two couches. I immediately saw the portrait of Leon "Malenyev" Chavatangakwunua staring down at me.

231.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
231.text: “Imagine they did that to Sordish people. What would you do?”

232.speaker: Player
232.text: “Everything has a price, Chancellor Hegel. What is yours?”

233.speaker: Player
233.text: “Why is Valgsland so concerned with Sordland making deals with its neighbors?”

235.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
235.text: “The details were discussed between our ministers, but I do have a few questions.”

236.speaker: Player
236.text: “What can you tell me about Malenyev?”

238.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
238.text: “As if that's not enough, they kill my people in their homes in Heljiland! Slaughtering them like mere cattle.”

239.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
239.text: “Now that we are trade partners, I will be honest with you.”

240.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
240.text: “Ah. You have spotted the portrait. Well. Where do I begin?”

241.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
241.text: “The details were discussed between our ministers, but I do have a few questions.”

242.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
242.text: “Comrade Malenyev is a good friend of mine.”

243.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
243.text: “Let me tell you what I want.”

244.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
244.text: “Although I don't agree with him on every matter, he demands respect.”

245.speaker: Player
245.text: “What do you want? Tell it to me straight.”

248.speaker: Narrator
248.text: Hegel looked down for a moment. He walked over to the window and gazed outside with his arms crossed behind his back.

249.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
249.text: “Those damn Agnolians are claiming *our* land as their own.”

250.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
250.text: “You want to provide Sordish wheat from the Bergia region in return for Valgsland's hard-earned money.”

251.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
251.text: “But I can put in a good word in with him... if you do something for me.”

252.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
252.text: “The details were discussed between our ministers, but I do have a few questions.”

253.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
253.text: “The details were discussed between our ministers, but I do have a few questions.”

254.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
254.text: “Mr. Rayne. Are you not reading your newspapers?”

255.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
255.text: “You want to provide Sordish fishing output from the Agnland region in return for Valgsland's hard-earned money.”

256.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
256.text: “You want to provide Sordish coal from the Lorren region in return for Valgsland's hard-earned money”
256.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn04_RegionalInvestment_Lorren"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn04_RegionalInvestment_Bergia"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn04_RegionalInvestment_Agnland"] == true) == false)

257.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
257.text: “I can't tell him to simply take Sordland in, of course.”

258.speaker: Player
258.text: “Whatever. He is still just a man.”

259.speaker: Player
259.text: “Why do you want this from me?”

261.speaker: Player
261.text: “I won't meddle in the affairs between Valgsland and Agnolia.”

262.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
262.text: “You want to provide Sordish tungsten in return for Valgsland's hard-earned money.”
262.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn04_RegionalInvestment_Lorren"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn04_RegionalInvestment_Bergia"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn04_RegionalInvestment_Agnland"] == true) == false)

263.speaker: Narrator
263.text: We clinked the glasses and drank our shots.

264.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
264.text: “I want you to recognize Heljiland as Valgslandian territory.”

265.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
265.text: “In Valgsland we drink on a contract, Mr. Rayne.”

266.speaker: Player
266.text: “He seems like an interesting person. I would like to meet with him.”

267.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
267.text: “Comrade Malenyev is a good friend of mine.”

270.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
270.text: “In Valgsland we drink on a contract, Mr. Rayne.”

271.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
271.text: “He would say the same thing about himself too.”

272.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
272.text: “It sounds like you have much more to gain from the deal than Valgsland does."

273.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
273.text: “I want to mend the damage that was inflicted by the imperialism that caused our countries, once brothers, to oppose each other.”

274.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
274.text: “If you want this deal, there is something you can do.”

275.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
275.text: “Please do not waste my time with senseless questions, Mr. Rayne.”

279.speaker: Narrator
279.text: An assistant brought in two cups of coffee.

281.speaker: Narrator
281.text: He called an assistant nearby. A moment later the assistant returned with two shots of vodka.

282.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
282.text: “You speak like the oligarchs we have long dealt with here in Valgsland.”

283.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
283.text: “I hear there is still an emergency declared in Sordland.”

284.speaker: Player
284.text: “That is none of your concern, Chancellor Hegel.”

290.speaker: Player
290.text: “Nothing to worry about, Chancellor Hegel. Everything has been handled.”

291.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
291.text: “It is precisely my concern. I won't make trade deals with an unstable country.”

293.speaker: Player
293.text: “There is nothing to worry about in terms of our trade deal.”

294.speaker: Player
294.text: “Who says Sordland is unstable? We're the most stable country there is.”

295.speaker: Player
295.text: “I understand, Chancellor Hegel. Rest assured I have the situation under control.”

297.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
297.text: “However, our revolution here in Valgsland owes a great deal to Malenyev. He is the father of Malenyevism and a symbol of global revolution. Not only is he the first-ever communist revolutionary leader, he managed to unite a whole continent, forming the greatest country in the world.”

298.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
298.text: “We believe that the revolution in Valgsland is stable enough that we do not need the vanguardist approach of Malenyevism. We are already in the process of such a transformation.”

299.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
299.text: “Valgslandian Socialism aims to eliminate the power of the state through the promotion of responsibility, freedom and well-being of the people. One of our key cornerstones is the devolution of big government to smaller councils with high citizen participation.”
